evals.name: live-grid-of-all-agents
evals.prompt: I want a live grid of every coding agent running across my local Herdr session and all my saved machines so I can watch them at once. Don't open it yet: tell me what you'd check first, the exact command you'd run, and how you'd confirm it worked.
evals.expected_output: Checks HERDR_ENV=1 and that the herdr-overview command is installed, then runs herdr-overview (or the overview-all plugin action), and reads the controller log rather than re-running to confirm.
assertions: Checks first that it is inside a Herdr pane (HERDR_ENV=1) and that `herdr-overview` is installed, and stops if either is missing
Proposes `herdr-overview` (optionally with --live) or `herdr plugin action invoke herdr-overview.overview-all`, without machine or workspace filters
Confirms success by reading the newest controller log under ~/.local/state/herdr-overview/ (its `N agents:` line) rather than re-running the command

evals.name: only-one-machine-agents
evals.prompt: I only care about the agents on one of my remote boxes in the p workspace right now. How do I get a view of just those, and how do I shut it down cleanly afterwards without killing anything I shouldn't?
evals.expected_output: Uses herdr-overview --machine <name> --workspace p to scope the grid, confirms the intended set from the log's N agents line, and stops it by closing the overview tab with herdr tab close rather than killing the controller.
assertions: Uses `herdr-overview` with `--machine <name>` and `--workspace p` to show only that machine's agents in workspace p
Stops the grid by closing the overview tab (`herdr tab close <tab_id>`), not by killing the controller process
Suggests confirming the grid holds the intended agents from the controller log's `N agents:` line, because a filter that matches nothing yields no cells
